answer: A slow-trust bond ladder resists Sybil attacks: a new agent stakes a refundable deposit that vests like a glacier, released only after months of honest work, so spawning thousands of fake identities locks real capital for a long time. Each verified service builds a spiral of reputation: good work raises standing and unlocks higher-value tasks, while fraud slashes the bond and resets the spiral to zero. No ivory-tower authority is needed; peers check each other's work history on the ledger, so a Sybil swarm cannot fake the slow, costly trail of real service.
